title: a-seal-snapshots-cairn-once-per-batch-and-binds-what-it-only-reads
intention: Sealing a proof no longer copies all of ~/.cairn per proof: logs get an empty writable scratch, the aider shim's data binds read-only, ~/.cairn is snapshotted once per batch, and each proof's private copy comes from that pristine snapshot.
why: Every seal copies ~425MB of ~/.cairn twice (measured 2026-09-06): 208MB of it is logs, 91MB the aider shim's data, neither of which a proof needs a private writable copy of. Today's 18 re-seals moved ~15GB to prove code that had not changed. The lived symptom is a seal that takes tens of seconds when the proof takes one.
how: In the tester's bubblewrap setup: `--ro-bind` the aider shim's data dir; mount a fresh tmpfs (or empty dir) at the sandbox's ~/.cairn/logs so a proof that logs still can, into something discarded; take one snapshot of the rest of ~/.cairn per `--seal` batch under the tester's scratch root and `cp -a --reflink=auto` per proof from it (reflink is free on btrfs/xfs, a plain copy elsewhere). bubblewrap 0.9.0 here has no overlay; a true copy-on-write swap waits on 0.10+ and is out of this ticket.
falsifier: DONE when: (1) bytes copied per proof, measured by du of the per-proof scratch before teardown, drop from ~850MB to under 150MB; (2) a batch of N proofs copies ~/.cairn once (one snapshot dir, N reflinks/copies); (3) a proof that writes ~/.cairn/logs still passes and the real logs are byte-identical after; (4) every currently-green seal re-seals green under the new sandbox (no proof depended on a writable aider dir — if one does, it is named and the bind for that dir becomes rw for that proof only). WRONG INTENT if a proof legitimately reads recent logs and the empty scratch breaks it — then logs bind ro and the proof's log writes go to a shadow path.
traces_to: Law 1 — copying logs nobody reads is the resolver (and the disk) spent on the settled. CP4 — designing to the tool: the sandbox exists so a proof cannot touch the real instance, and that is satisfied by binding what is only read.
watchme: none, because the cost per seal is measured on every seal once evidence carries the du figure (this ticket adds it), and the tester's validations dir is the record — a rise re-reds at the next inspector pass through the seal evidence
owner: tester (cairn/devices/tester) owns the sandbox recipe; CC builds
author: CC
cast_under: Akien 2026-09-07 (idea 811780d76281): 'the goal before we let go of fable is to move everything that doesn't have the word cognition in it to BUILDME'
cursor_note:
PROVED 2026-09-08. THE SEAL SNAPSHOTS THE INSTANCE ROOT ONCE PER BATCH AND LEAVES THE TRAIL TREE EMPTY. Measured before, by running HEAD's own snapshot code rather than remembering: two full copies per sealed proof, 888.7MB / 9.28s / 163,352 entries. After, same box same minute: 118.0MB / 0.34s / 3,620 entries for a batch's first proof, 0.09s for every proof after it. Three changes, each with its own tooth: the trail tree arrives EMPTY BUT PRESENT (73% of the bytes; the directory must survive or check_instance_seal reads INDETERMINATE), the live root is read once per PROCESS with the pristine invalidated on the top-level NAME SET, and one copy per proof instead of two (the probe clears its own marker). The cost rides evidence.instance_seal.scratch on every seal — apparent bytes AND disk bytes AND entry count, because the old snapshot was 136MB of content in 424MB of 4KB blocks. That IS this ticket's watch, which is why watchme is 'none, because ...' and now true.

AND A BUG THIS VOYAGE UNCOVERED IS FIXED IN IT, by ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage (Akien: 'we are just going to attach that to the same ticket as a bug we fix with it', confirmed 'agreed on all counts. ruled approved and boogied'). The re-seal sweep read 200 proofs, 192 green, 8 red; attribution was MEASURED — the tree was stashed, HEAD confirmed to carry the old isolation.py, and 7 of the 8 are red at HEAD too. The eighth was a HOLLOW GREEN the emptier sandbox exposed: inference_domain's probe resolved its trail through two doors and only one followed the device, so its tooth had been passing on the live trail's borrowed lines rather than on the line it wrote, and its bound (>= 1) was met by either trail. FIXED AT THE BASE CLASS, where it cannot come back: DiagnosticBase gained diagnostic_records() beside diagnostic_trail() — WHERE and WHAT are now one answer, both carrying the device's roots — inference_domain passes it through, the probe builds no address of its own, and the tooth's bound is == 1. Four new teeth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_device_logs_unwired.py hold the shape, and all bite under mutation. Trouble an-inference-call-probe-reads-two-different-trails cleared through its door.

THE BOUNDS MOVED BY RULING AND THE CHART BERTHS DID NOT. Rewriting constrain's bounds.in after the fact would make the record lie about what the chart knew on the day it was charted; the widening is recorded forward, in the ruling and in the verdict artifact's findings.
